findings.trigger: cogs.auto_action_monitor or cogs.translation_monitor fails to load (its setup() raises, or an import inside it fails). py-cord reports that as discord.ExtensionFailed / ExtensionNotFound / NoEntryPointError, which descend from DiscordException -> Exception and are in NONE of the six types caught here (IOError, OSError, PermissionError, RuntimeError, docker APIError/DockerException). The exception escapes the step; per the comment in power.py:64-67 the sequence and its caller have no handler, so every step after it is skipped: no command sync, no stale-panel cleanup, no dynamic cooldowns, no scheduler, no update notice, no member count. The bot is online, the status messages work (docker_control loaded), scheduled tasks silently never fire, and 'Initialization complete' is never logged. The comment at :48 says 'We don't raise here to allow other extensions to load' - for the exception load_extension actually raises, the code does raise.
findings.suggestion: Catch discord.ExtensionError (the base of ExtensionFailed, ExtensionNotFound, NoEntryPointError, ExtensionAlreadyLoaded) in addition, or catch Exception here and keep the explicit re-raise for cogs.docker_control. Consider a handler in run_startup_sequence that logs a step's failure and continues with the next step, so that one nicety cannot take the scheduler with it.
findings.unsure_why: The py-cord exception hierarchy is from memory, not from the material; startup_steps/sequence.py is not in my material, only power.py's comment that it has no handler.

findings.trigger: A slash command raises a DDC exception (e.g. DockerConnectionError). py-cord's hooked_wrapped_callback wraps everything raised inside a command callback in ApplicationCommandInvokeError(exc), which IS an ApplicationCommandError. So the exception arrives in the first branch (:114-116), not in the else branch the comment at :118-124 describes. Consequences: (a) the user receives _('Error during execution: {error}') with str(error) = 'Application Command raised an exception: DockerConnectionError: <original text>' - exactly the path/URL/config-value leak that :126-131 says the generic message exists to prevent; (b) the log line at :116 has no exc_info, so the traceback of the real exception is not logged at all - only the branch that (in practice) is never reached logs one. The else branch is reached only for exceptions raised before invocation (checks, conversion) that are not ApplicationCommandError subclasses.
findings.suggestion: Unwrap ApplicationCommandInvokeError (error.original) and treat that case like the else branch: log with exc_info=True and answer with the generic message. Keep the readable message only for genuine ApplicationCommandError subclasses (CheckFailure, conversion errors). Fix the comment.
findings.unsure_why: The wrapping in ApplicationCommandInvokeError is py-cord behaviour I know from memory and cannot verify in the material.

findings.trigger: The bot is in a guild but compute_unique_member_count returns 0 (no status channels configured yet on a fresh install, or the member cache not filled) and the snapshot has no previous count (0). resolved_count becomes 1 (:69), which differs from previous (0), so :76-82 publish and PERSIST a member count of 1 with source='status_channels' and description 'Unique members across all status channels' - a number nobody measured, recorded as if it had been. _recalculate_goal then sets goal_requirement and difficulty_bin for a one-member server (the cheapest bin). SPEC Z7 states that this number determines what the next mech level costs. The WARNING at :68 says 'using fallback' but the persisted record claims a measurement.
findings.suggestion: When resolved_count <= 0 and there is no previous count, do not persist and do not recalculate the goal; leave the snapshot for the next start or for the cog's own refresh. If 1 must be written, record source='fallback' so the file says what it is.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether the cog refreshes the member count later (which would limit the damage to the time until the next refresh) or whether the level-1 count is locked once written, as the lock emoji at :75 suggests.

findings.trigger: cog.channel_server_message_ids is written to disk by cog._persist_tracked_message_ids (:65) - if that is JSON, its keys come back as STRINGS after a restart. bot.get_channel('123456') always returns None, so every start logs 'Donation panel ... stays: channel ... is not reachable' at INFO (a misleading reason) and the stale panel with its dead 'Broadcast Donation' button is never removed - the exact situation this step was added for on 2026-09-23. It also has no try/except around the loop: a tracked value that is not a dict (legacy format) raises AttributeError at :40, escapes the step and, like F1, stops the steps after it (cooldowns, scheduler, member count).
findings.suggestion: Convert the key with int(channel_id) before get_channel (guarded for non-numeric keys), and wrap the loop body so one bad entry is logged and skipped rather than aborting the startup.
findings.unsure_why: The cog's loader is not in my material; if it converts keys to int when reading the file, the first half does not apply. The second half depends on the format of the tracked values.

findings.trigger: POST /api/groups with a body that names the group but omits 'containers' (e.g. {"name": "media", "active": false} from a page that only wants to flip the group's switch). The comment at :123-126 explains that active and allowed_actions pass None so 'the service keeps what the group has' - but containers is passed as [] ('or []'). Depending on the service, the group either loses all its members and the page gets {success: true}, or the save is refused for having no members. Both are wrong for a caller that said nothing about the members, and the first is silent.
findings.suggestion: Pass data.get('containers') through as None when the key is absent (and only [] when the caller sends []), and let the service keep the members in the None case - the same rule the two fields below it already follow. Also pass the same value to _make_members_steerable.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see the page's JS nor group_service.save_group; if every caller always sends the full container list and the service refuses [], the damage is a visible refusal, not a silent loss.

findings.trigger: _make_members_steerable decides 'DDC already has a configuration for this container' with its own path rule: (config_dir/'containers'/f'{name}.json').exists(). The actual file name is decided by container_config_save_service.save_container_config (:103), which is a second place. If the two ever differ (sanitised or lower-cased file names, a different directory), exists() is False for a container that IS configured, and every save of a group containing it overwrites its configuration with active=False, allowed_actions=[] - the operator's running container loses its buttons and its permissions with {success: true} and only an INFO line 'joined a group and was given a configuration'.
findings.suggestion: Ask the save service (or the container config loader) whether a configuration exists rather than re-deriving the path here; at minimum, never write when a config with that container_name can be loaded.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see container_config_save_service; if it writes exactly <name>.json under config_dir/containers, the two places agree today and this is only a drift risk.

findings.trigger: The group has already been saved (:126-131) when _make_members_steerable runs. The except at :88 lists five types; docker.errors.DockerException (raised e.g. when the Docker socket cannot be reached while creating the client) is a direct Exception subclass and is not among them. Likewise save_container_config (:103) is expected to return False on failure but any exception it raises is uncaught. The request then ends in a 500 - the panel reports the save as failed although the group is stored. The comment at :89-91 promises 'A daemon that does not answer must not cost the operator what he just typed'; a 500 makes him retype or believe it is not there.
findings.suggestion: Catch Exception around the whole steerability pass (log at WARNING, return) - the group is saved, and this is precisely the 'nicety must not fail the main result' case - or at least add docker.errors.DockerException and wrap the per-container save.
findings.unsure_why: get_docker_containers_live returns an (containers, error) pair and may already swallow Docker errors internally; I cannot see it or the save service.

findings.trigger: test_translation re-implements the DeepL/Google/Microsoft HTTP calls inside the route (:285-350) instead of calling services.translation's translation service that the bot uses. Any difference between the two - a Microsoft regional key that needs Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Region, the DeepL free/pro URL choice, formality or glossary options, how the key is resolved, the SSRF allow-list - makes the panel's 'Test' button report success while the bot's translations fail (or the reverse). The operator uses this button to confirm the configuration the bot will run with; it confirms a different implementation.
findings.suggestion: Route the test through the same service method the translation_monitor cog uses (a synchronous wrapper or a one-shot call), so the test exercises the real path. If the urllib re-implementation must stay because of gevent, cover the equivalence with a test that fails when the two diverge.
findings.unsure_why: services/translation is not in my material; I cannot tell how far the two implementations already differ today.

findings.trigger: settings.deepl_api_url is operator-configured. If it is not https or not on the allow-list (a typo, http://, a proxy), _api_post returns (400, None) and the route answers 'DeepL API error: HTTP 400' (:303) - the operator reads that DeepL rejected the request and checks the key, while the real reason (URL blocked by DDC) is only a WARNING in the log.
findings.suggestion: Return a distinct marker from _api_post for the blocked case (or raise) and answer with 'The configured API URL is not an allowed translation endpoint'.

findings.trigger: build_runtime calls ensure_token_security before the bot exists. Its except lists RuntimeError, OSError, ValueError, AttributeError, TypeError. token.py:79-91 documents that this project's crypto/config errors (TokenEncryptionError -> ConfigServiceError -> DDCBaseException) match none of these and that the same tuple-shaped gap had to be fixed twice already (E7, E8). If auto_encrypt_token_on_startup raises any DDCBaseException (or a cryptography error) for a config it cannot handle, the exception escapes build_runtime, the process dies before connecting, and the container restart-loops - the opposite of what the comment at :204 promises ('must never abort the startup').
findings.suggestion: Catch Exception here (with the same justification token.py gives: this is an optional nicety whose contract is 'return False on any failure'), log at WARNING, return False.
findings.unsure_why: utils/token_security.auto_encrypt_token_on_startup is not in my material; it may already catch its own errors, in which case the gap is theoretical.

findings.trigger: delete_group answers 404 for EVERY refusal from the service, not only 'no such group' - a failed file write or a refusal because tasks still reference the group comes back as 404 too. The comment at :168-169 reasons only about the 'not there' case. rename_group (:157-158) distinguishes the two by matching the error text; delete does not. A page that treats 404 as 'already gone' removes the row while the group still exists after reload.
findings.suggestion: Use the same distinction as rename_group (better: a typed reason on the result instead of matching the message text, which is itself a second place that can drift).
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether group_service.delete_group can fail for any reason other than a missing group, nor how the page treats a 404.

findings.trigger: POST /api/groups with allowed_actions of any non-list type (a string 'start,stop', a dict, a number) is silently converted to None = 'keep what the group has', and the response is {success: true}. The caller's answer is dropped and the caller is told it was taken.
findings.suggestion: Refuse with 400 when allowed_actions is present but not a list; only an absent key should mean 'keep'.

findings.trigger: start_scheduler_service() returns False. One WARNING covers two opposite states: 'could not be started' (no scheduled task will ever run) 'or was already running' (everything is fine). An operator whose scheduler failed reads a line that offers 'already running' as an explanation and looks no further; the failure is a warning, not an error.
findings.suggestion: Ask the service which it is (an is_running check before starting, or a richer return) and log the failure at ERROR with its reason, the already-running case at INFO.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see start_scheduler_service; if it logs the reason itself at ERROR, this only duplicates a clear message.

notes: save_group carries F5, F6, F7 and F12 (F6/F7 live in _make_members_steerable, which is not a plan name); test_translation carries F8 and F9. Not findings for lack of a trigger I can state: (1) events.py:76 - whether str(ctx.command) equals the bare name for a py-cord SlashCommand I cannot verify; if it does not, is_donation_command is never true and donation commands may be answered twice. (2) toggle_pair:126-128 resets auto-disable on every toggle, also when disabling; the comment says 'if user re-enables'. Harmless because a disabled pair is not used. (3) group_routes.py:158 and delete_group: matching the service's error TEXT to choose the status code is a second copy of a string that may drift. (4) list_groups catches only OSError; a corrupt groups file (JSONDecodeError) would give a non-JSON 500 unless the service handles it - visible either way. (5) save_api_key: an empty field CLEARS the key, whereas B8 says an empty bot-token field means keep; different endpoint, documented in its docstring, but worth one look at what the panel posts. (6) synchronize_commands_step logs 'No guild ID configured, skipping' then 'synchronization process completed' at INFO - a fresh install without guild_id gets no slash commands and a log that reads as success. (7) send_update_notification_step catches a narrow tuple; if the notifier lets an aiohttp/urllib/JSON error through, the member count step after it is skipped. (8) ensure_log_files:186 says discord.log 'keeps everything' while the handler is at INFO (no DEBUG). (9) _make_members_steerable checks the RAW request names against the host, not the names the service accepted; if the service normalises names, a member the operator typed with different case/whitespace stays 'missing'. (10) resolve_timezone falls back to UTC, not to the 'Europe/Berlin' default, when the configured zone is invalid - documented in its docstring; a scheduled task then runs at the wrong hour with only a startup WARNING, if the scheduler uses this zone (not visible). SPEC contradictions: none found in this section; Z9 holds in token.py (the token itself never reaches a log line).
